_note: First-aid guidance only — reviewed-pending by Dr. Suhasini. The clinic has no separate after-hours number (confirm).

urgentWarning.en: Go to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately if you have swelling that is spreading to the eye or neck, difficulty breathing or swallowing, a high fever with facial swelling, uncontrolled bleeding, or a head or jaw injury.
urgentWarning.te: కంటి లేదా మెడ వరకు వ్యాపిస్తున్న వాపు, శ్వాస లేదా మింగడంలో ఇబ్బంది, అధిక జ్వరం, ఆగని రక్తస్రావం, లేదా తల/దవడ గాయం ఉంటే వెంటనే దగ్గరలోని ఆసుపత్రి అత్యవసర విభాగానికి వెళ్ళండి.

duringHours.en: During clinic hours, call us first — we'll do our best to see you the same day.
duringHours.te: క్లినిక్ సమయాల్లో ముందుగా మాకు కాల్ చేయండి.

afterHours.en: Outside clinic hours, send us a WhatsApp message and we'll get back to you when the clinic opens. For anything serious, go to a hospital emergency department.
afterHours.te: క్లినిక్ సమయం తర్వాత వాట్సాప్ సందేశం పంపండి. తీవ్రమైన సమస్య అయితే ఆసుపత్రికి వెళ్ళండి.

steps.en: Rinse your mouth gently with warm salt water.
Use floss to remove any food caught between the teeth.
A cold compress on the outside of the cheek may ease swelling.
Take a pain reliever you have safely used before, as directed on the pack. Do not place tablets on the gum.
Call the clinic — lasting pain usually needs treatment.
Act quickly — the sooner you are seen, the better the chance of saving the tooth.
Pick the tooth up by the crown (the white part). Don't touch the root.
If it's dirty, rinse briefly with milk or clean water. Don't scrub it.
If you can, gently push it back into its socket and bite on a clean cloth to hold it.
If not, keep it in a small container of milk or inside the cheek (not for young children) and come to the clinic or an emergency department straight away.
Knocked-out milk teeth should not be put back — but do bring your child in to be checked.
Rinse with warm water and save any broken pieces.
Apply gentle pressure with gauze if there is bleeding.
Use a cold compress to reduce swelling.
Call the clinic for an appointment.
Rinse with warm salt water several times a day.
Do not apply heat to the outside of the face.
Call the clinic the same day — infections need prompt treatment.
If swelling spreads towards the eye or neck, or you feel unwell with a fever, go to a hospital emergency department.
